# Data story — Style Prompt

> A chart that tells a story in one take: real-looking numbers drawn mark by mark on cream paper by a red–blue pencil, with handwritten notes pinned to the marks. The camera starts in an extreme close-up on the first dot while its note is written, pulls back as the axis grows out of that dot and the chart's serif headline typesets above, then tracks the pencil as the dots land faster and faster; a record tears through the top of the frame, the pencil flinches and flips to its red end, and the story ends on a dashed empty cell for the value nobody knows yet.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

**The chart is the film.** Every mark is a number and every movement is a chart operation: a mark lands, an axis grows, a note is pinned, the frame breaks, an empty cell waits. The paper is one sheet under one camera; there are no cuts. Three layers make it a story rather than an infographic: a **human scale** (handwritten notes on the marks: "Minggu 1 — sekeranjang."), a **performer** (the physical red–blue pencil that draws every line and taps every dot), and **rhythm** (the data's density sets the pace: sparse marks land slowly, dense ones hurry).

Pick the chart the data asks for: categories or rankings → bars or a bar race; two measures → a scatter where one dot can be a character; parts of a whole → a unit or waffle chart; before → after → a slope chart; change over time → a dot-and-line series (the example). The craft below works for all of them.

Not a dashboard (one idea at a time, one chart on screen), not a stage talk with chart slides (never cut to a new slide), not decoration (no chart without numbers), not a counter animation (numbers are marks in space, not big ticking digits).

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Paper**: warm cream with soft cloudy tone and fine fibres, painted once from `--latar` (a 960×540 canvas turned into a full-frame image), plus a faint dot grid every 24 world px that moves with the camera and keeps its dots small when zoomed (radius 1.43/√zoom px). The dot grid is what makes camera motion legible.
- **Ink**: the axes 1.4–1.6 px, the series line 2.4 px with round joins, gridlines 1 px in a pale ink mix, the drop line dashed 3/5 in soft ink. Strokes are world-space SVG; their width scales with the camera, like ink on a photographed sheet.
- **Marks**: data dots r 6 with a 1.5 px ink ring, so pale values stay visible on cream. A landing dot pops to 1.43× over 0.25 s and sends a thin ripple in its own fill colour (to 3× r over 0.6 s, 6.5× r for the first and last mark); no ripples when marks arrive less than 0.2 s apart.
- **Pencil lines**: every annotation stroke (ring, leader, doodle, the empty cell) is a hand line: a low-frequency wobble perpendicular to the path (±0.4 × width), a second thinner pass offset by under 1 px at 40 % opacity, round caps, written on along its length. Rings are **un-closed**: 1.12 turns, radius 2.3× the dot, slightly elliptical and widening as they go. Leaders are quadratic curves bent 0.22 of their length.
- **Handwriting**: Caveat in the pencil's colour, each glyph rotated ±1.7° and shifted ±0.75 px off the baseline, revealed left to right while the pencil tip dances over the x-height. Small doodles after a note (three rain strokes, a wave, a heart) are drawn the same way.
- **The red–blue pencil**: a long hex body, front half `--utama`, back half `--aksen`, a light stripe and a dark stripe along it, a sharpened wood cone with a scalloped paint edge, a graphite tip tinted by the lead. Only the tip end shows, entering from the lower right at 35–58°; its shadow is a blurred silhouette that drifts farther (3 + 70 × lift × scale px) and fades as the pencil lifts.
- **Layout**: a plot box fixed in world space; early notes in a **memory zone** where the data will never go; every note pinned in data space (the mark's value plus a pixel offset); the chart's headline in world space above the plot; the bottom 180 px of the screen for the figure caption.

## 3. Colour logic

- **Colour encodes one thing: the value.** A diverging ramp centred on a meaningful reference value with a symmetric span: below the centre the dot fill mixes `--utama` into the paper (up to 75 %), above it `--aksen` (75 % at one span, deeper beyond). Pale values stay pale; never stretch the ramp to make a change look bigger. Data with no natural centre uses one sequential ramp of `--utama`.
- **The two leads mean something**: `--utama-di-latar` (blue in the film) for memories and human notes, `--aksen-di-latar` (red) for records, warnings and the unknown next value. A change of lead marks a turn in the story.
- `--latar` is the paper and the caption band (94 %) behind the figure caption; `--teks` is the ink: axes, series line, dot rings, headline, caption; `--teks-redup` is printed small matter: tick labels, the mono kicker, the subtitle, the drop line. `--latar-2` is reserved for a second sheet (an inset table or a pasted card) when a story needs one.
- `--utama` and `--aksen` also paint the pencil's two halves and their graphite tips; `--teks-di-utama` / `--teks-di-aksen` only if a label is ever set on a solid colour field (the look avoids it).
- Fixed in every brand: pencil wood `#e3c79c` / `#c9a774`, graphite `#3a3733`, the pencil shadow `#46321e`, the body highlight white. Grid dots (`--teks` 9 %) and gridlines (`--teks` 13 %) are mixed into `--latar`, so a dark brand gets a blackboard with chalk-light ink and still reads.

## 4. Type

- `--font-judul` carries the chart's own headline, set in world space above the plot (Libre Baskerville 400 at 62 world px, about 96 px on screen at the 1.55× pull-back), typeset letter by letter, and the end card's name (46 world px). It fades out while the camera is close and returns with the full view.
- `--font-isi` carries the **figure caption**, the film's only voice: 40 px on screen at x 140, baseline about 980, one line of at most about 10 words, left-aligned, over the paper band; and the end card's lines (24 world px).
- Look fonts that brands do not replace: `--font-tangan` Caveat 700 at 30 world px for every note; `--font-angka` IBM Plex Mono 400 for ticks (17 world px), sticky axis labels (20 px on screen), the kicker (18 px), value labels beside the first and last mark ("36 buku") and the contact line.
- When the brand has no fonts: a text serif for both (Libre Baskerville, Cormorant Garamond 500, Playfair Display for a louder headline). A grotesk brand font works for the caption; keep Caveat and the mono.
- Leave room: notes are short (under 25 characters), so a wider brand font in the caption wraps to two lines at most.

## 5. Motion quality

- **The rhythm of the data is the rhythm of the film.** Marks land on a grid that subdivides as the data densifies: 0.5 s apart (quarters), then 0.25 s (eighths), then 0.125 s (sixteenths). To accelerate, divide the beat; never change the tempo smoothly.
- **Drawing a mark**: the pencil draws the line segment from the previous dot over `min(0.45 s, 0.8 × gap)`, hops at the end (lift 0.22 in the last 30 %), and the dot lands on the beat.
- **A note**: ring 0.12–0.2 s, leader 0.08–0.12 s, writing at about 25 characters per second, doodle 0.06 s per stroke. The pencil scribbles (lift 0.04–0.09) while writing.
- **Pencil acting**: lifts before each tap and lands with its shadow meeting the tip; leaves the frame toward the lower right when it has nothing to draw for more than 1.6 s (0.9 s out, 0.9 s back); its posture steepens from 0.62 to 1.0 rad in dense passages so the body never lies across fresh dots. It can **flinch** (recoil 14/16 px in 0.12 s, then freeze with a 1 px tremble for half a beat), **flip** end over end to the other lead (0.26–0.5 s, pivoting about 180 px up the body, `eio`), and **exit**, handing the story to the viewer.
- **Typesetting**: each glyph fades in over 4 glyph-steps and settles 10 px (headline); the subtitle without the rise.
- **Caption**: the hairline rule opens (0.25 s), words appear on their times (0.125 s fade, 6 px rise, 0.28 s apart at reading pace), the caption holds at least 1.8 s, then flips up 26 px and fades in 0.3 s.
- **No fades to blank, no dissolves.** Transitions are chart operations: an axis growing, a pull-back, a frame break, a cell widening into the next frame. The ending holds still at least 2 s.

## 6. Camera grammar

A 2D camera `{x, y, zoom, roll}` over one sheet of paper; one take. Zoom interpolates in log space. Moves ease with cubic in-out unless noted.

| Move | Expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Extreme close-up (≈3.9×) on one mark, drifting in to 3.95× while its note is written | One fact, one life | the first customer, the first day, a single case, a named person |
| Pull back to ≈1.55× over 1.7 s as the drop line becomes the axis and the headline typesets | The frame arrives with the unit | naming the measure, widening a claim |
| Track the pencil (2.25× → 2.0×): newest mark at about 38 % of the width (230 px lead), data held mid-frame, the x axis kept near the caption | Progress: the past behind, the future ahead | a series in time, a queue, a race |
| Slow pull-out and a Dutch angle creeping to −1.2° as the data densifies and climbs | Escalation | growth, a rush, a debt |
| Punch-in +11 % over 2 frames, shake 12 px decaying as e^(−6t), settling over 0.8 s | Surprise, a broken frame | an outlier, a record, a crash |
| Pull back and pan to the full view (≈1.3×) with the empty next cell in frame | The whole, and what is still open | the call to action, a verdict, "what next?" |
| Locked-off | The transformation is the movement | a morph (bars → units), a slow reading |

When the real y axis scrolls off-screen, its labels pin to the left edge over a paper strip (frozen pane), so values stay readable while tracking.

## 7. Native moves

- **One mark = one fact.** The film opens on a single dot in extreme close-up: the pencil has just tapped it (ripple), it is ringed, a leader rises and the note is written while the camera drifts in; its value sits beside it in mono. *Fits content like:* the first week a shop opened; a creator's first upload with 41 views; the first student who signed up for a class; "the day she was born" in a family story.
- **Axes grow with the story.** No axis until the unit is named: a dashed drop line falls from the first mark and becomes the x axis, the headline typesets above, and the grid, y axis and labels grow in when the caption says what a dot is. *Fits content like:* orders per week; subscribers per month; minutes of practice per day for a course; a town's rainfall in a short documentary.
- **Pinned annotations.** Notes ring their mark, curve a leader to a quiet zone and are written in pencil; blue for memories and human moments, red for records and warnings; a small doodle (rain, a wave, a heart) carries the feeling. *Fits content like:* "Minggu 7 — hujan." under a dip; a product feature on its launch week; "exam week" on a study log; the move to a new city in a biography.
- **Track the pencil.** The camera follows the newest mark while the data rhythm accelerates from quarters to sixteenths and the pencil hurries, steepens and trembles. *Fits content like:* sales climbing after a review went viral; a channel's weekly views; a class's attendance across a term; the days of a long journey.
- **Breaking the frame.** The record pierces the chart's top edge; the edge tears with frayed ends and stays torn as a scar; the camera punches in and shakes; the pencil flinches, freezes, flips to its red end and writes "rekor!". *Fits content like:* a sold-out week; a video that broke a creator's chart; a record score in a school competition; the flood year in a village story.
- **The empty next cell.** After the last mark the red pencil draws a dashed slot for the value nobody knows yet; it widens into the end card (frame within frame) with the name, place and contact. *Fits content like:* "Minggu depan?" for a reading bike; next month's pre-orders; the next episode of a series; tomorrow's reading in an experiment.

## 8. Pitfalls

- **Performance (live preview).** The world (SVG plus a few world-space HTML texts) repaints on every camera frame, so keep it light: under about 300 nodes, no filters, masks only on small strokes, generated geometry rather than hand-drawn path data. Paint the paper once to an image under the world; draw the dot grid as a CSS radial gradient (only its radius variable changes). Put the pencil and its shadow in their own composited layers (`will-change: transform`) with the shadow blur inside a static SVG filter; only the end-over-end flip changes them.
- **Honest numbers.** Bars and areas start at zero; a line may not, but say so. The ramp is centred on a stated reference and symmetric. Never invent a figure for a real business: ask for the data, and print the value that each note claims.
- **Collisions.** Notes pinned in data space collide with later data: keep early notes in the memory zone (above low early values, below high ones), keep notes under 25 characters, and right-align notes on the late side of the chart (the pencil then hops to the first letter before writing).
- **Text widths.** Handwriting reveals and the pencil tip depend on the text's width: measure it once fonts have loaded (`getComputedTextLength`), with a per-character estimate before that.
- **Small type.** Ticks and kickers are small by nature; everything the viewer must read (caption, card name, contact) stays at 40 px on screen or close to it at the final zoom.
- **Captions** never cover a signature operation (the frame break, the flip) or the last 2 s of silence on the end card.
- **Light brands.** A pale main colour fails as note ink: notes use `--utama-di-latar`, which falls back to the text colour; check that the pale pencil body still separates from white paper (the wood cone and stripes keep it legible).
- **First frame.** The film starts mid-gesture (a ringed dot, the pencil on the paper), never on blank paper.

## Measured from the reference

One shot, no cuts, 12 s; the paper takes 91 % of the frame (`#f3f2e9`), pale greys and ink 9 %; low motion energy (2.35), all of it camera drift, pencil and marks. The close-up holds about 1 s before the pull-back, the full view with the headline holds about 1.5 s, and tracking starts about 3 s in.

## Variation space

- Structures: a ranked race (bars climb and overtake; one bar is the character; a newcomer breaks the frame from below); a map that becomes a count (dots gather on a map, then fall into a unit chart in one morph); a before → after slope chart with one line left unfinished.
- Openings: the finished chart (the film works backwards); the object before the axis (a pencil drawing of the thing measured, a ticket, a shoe, becomes the first mark); the question first (an empty plot with only the unit and a handwritten question; the pencil hovers).
- Endings: one mark, close (end on a single value and its note); the headline revised (the pencil strikes a word of the title and writes the true one); the empty next cell (the example).
- Encoding morph: a staggered sweep (0.85 beat) turns dots into stripes or bars into units; notes fade as it passes and return as tiny pencil marks.
- Scale switch: one value → the series → a longer record, the axis rescaling in four eased ratchet steps; never extrapolate.

# Data story: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.6, medium 2.6, long 4.

## hook

- en: extreme close-up on the first mark; the pencil rings it and writes a handwritten note while the camera tilts up the leader
- id: close-up ekstrem pada titik pertama; pensil melingkarinya dan menulis catatan, kamera naik mengikuti garis tunjuk

## problem

- en: a dip in the line is ringed in pencil and gets a short note with a doodle under it; the camera holds
- id: titik yang turun dilingkari pensil, diberi catatan pendek dan coretan kecil di bawahnya; kamera diam

## fact

- en: pull back as the mark's drop line becomes the x axis; the chart's serif headline typesets above it
- id: kamera mundur, garis jatuh dari titik menjadi sumbu x; judul grafik diketik huruf demi huruf di atasnya

## step

- en: the pencil draws one segment and taps one dot per step, the camera tracking with the newest mark on the left third
- id: pensil menarik satu garis dan mengetuk satu titik per langkah, kamera mengikuti dengan titik terbaru di kiri

## compare

- en: two marks ringed in the two leads: a blue note for before, a red note for after, each on its own leader
- id: dua titik dilingkari dua warna pensil: catatan biru untuk sebelum, merah untuk sesudah, masing-masing bergaris tunjuk

## number

- en: dots land faster and faster; the record pierces the chart's top edge, the pencil flinches, flips to red and writes it
- id: titik mendarat makin cepat; rekor menembus tepi atas grafik, pensil kaget, berbalik ke ujung merah lalu menulisnya

## proof

- en: pull back to the whole series, every note still pinned to its value, the source named in mono under a hairline
- id: kamera mundur ke seluruh rangkaian, tiap catatan tetap di angkanya, sumber data ditulis mono di bawah garis tipis

## offer

- en: the mark that matters gets a red ring, a red handwritten note and its exact figure in mono beside it
- id: titik yang penting diberi lingkaran merah, catatan tangan merah, dan angkanya dalam huruf mono di sampingnya

## cta

- en: a dashed empty cell after the last mark widens into the end card with name, place and contact, held 2 s
- id: sel kosong putus-putus sesudah titik terakhir melebar jadi kartu penutup: nama, tempat, kontak, diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: full view of the finished chart, the dashed empty cell waiting for the next value with a handwritten question, held 2 s
- id: seluruh grafik yang selesai, sel kosong putus-putus menunggu angka berikutnya dengan pertanyaan tulisan tangan, diam 2 detik

      :root {

        --font-judul: "Libre Baskerville", "Noto Sans", serif; --font-isi: "Libre Baskerville", "Noto Sans", serif;

        --kayu: #e3c79c; --kayu-tua: #c9a774; --grafit: #3a3733; --bayang: #46321e; --kilau: #ffffff;
